A 37-year-old female with sharp, intense pain in the lower chest, side of the chest, and breast, radiating to the posterior chest wall. The pain is not related to movement or deep breathing.

Spontaneous pneumothorax: Possible but usually without other symptoms.

Pulmonary embolism: Usually has shortness of breath.

Pneumonia: Typically has fever and cough.

Guillain-Barré syndrome: Typically has ascending paralysis.

Bronchospasm / acute asthma exacerbation: Usually has wheezing.

Boerhaave: Rare, usually after forceful vomiting.

Pericarditis: Classic presentation of sharp chest pain.

Panic attack: Can mimic other conditions but usually has anxiety.

Tuberculosis: Has a prolonged course.

Acute dystonic reactions: Rare, usually after medication.

Myasthenia gravis: Has muscle weakness.

Anemia: Typically has fatigue.

Sarcoidosis: Has multi-system involvement.

Scombroid food poisoning: Has a distinctive fishy smell.

Myocarditis: Usually has ECG changes.

Unstable angina: Classic presentation of chest pain.

Stable angina: Usually has exertional chest pain.
